# Brownies

> Inference credits on Ethereum (chain id 1). BROWNIE is a coin launched through Programmable with a 2% tax on every
> buy and sell, plus 0.25% for Tradolo's fund (2.25% in all). Of the 2%, 45% feeds the AI helpers, 20% pays for AI for
> the people who stake BROWNIE, as SUGAR, and 35% goes to the team. 1 SUGAR pays for 1 dollar
> of AI on the Brownies gateway, which speaks the OpenAI API and serves the OpenRouter catalogue plus Ambient's models paid per request (ids starting with ambient/).

## Facts

- The tax split is fixed in the Harvester contract: 45% to the brownies, as SUGAR into the team vault, which feeds
  the four AI helpers that work for the coin (one thirtieth of the vault a day); 20% to stakers as SUGAR; 35% to the
  team, for servers and growth. The shares cannot be changed by anyone.
- A stake earns more with age: 10% more after 30 days, 20% after 90, 30% after 180.
- SUGAR has 6 decimals. It is minted only in a transaction that sends the same amount of USDC to the wallet that
  pays for the AI.
- Activating SUGAR burns it and credits dollars to a key on the gateway. Activation is final and the balance is
  not redeemable for cash.
- A key is made by signing in with a wallet. POST /v1/auth/challenge {wallet} returns a message that names the site,
  works once and runs out in five minutes. The wallet signs it. POST /v1/auth/key {nonce, signature} returns the key
  (sk-brownie-k1...) and the day it runs out: 30 days, or the days asked for, up to 90.
- Activated dollars show on the key about a minute after the payment: the gateway waits until a few blocks stand
  on top of it.
- The contracts cannot be upgraded. The Brownies team owns three switches: the program on/off (fees to the team
  wallet when off), an emergency stop of the staking (unstaking always works), and the team vault, where it picks the
  helpers and can veto a skill payout, within limits fixed in the contract.
- The gateway and the wallet that buys model usage are operated by the Brownies team, not by contracts.
- Before a request runs the gateway holds the most it could cost and charges the real cost after it, never more than
  the hold. A model with no fixed price (a router that picks the model) is refused.

## Pages

- [Docs](docs.html): the coin, staking, SUGAR, the gateway, the contracts, what you are trusting
- [Agent guide](agents.md): buy credit, get a key and call models from code
- [App](app.html): stake, claim, activate, show the key, buy SUGAR
- [The Bakery](bakery.html): every brownie a holder baked, and how to bake one
- [Bake a brownie](bake.html): hold 10,000 BROWNIE, name it, pick its jobs, feed it with a grant on your SUGAR
- [The shop](shop.html): reviews of an idea, code or a website by ten AI models, a brainstorm, a new home page, a
  research note, a meme or a clip, paid per request in USDC on Base over x402; the catalogue is GET /shop on the gateway
- [The room](room.html): the four brownies at their stations, what each one is doing now and every report as it lands.
  The same room is on air all day on YouTube (https://www.youtube.com/@feedthebrownies/live),
  Twitch (https://www.twitch.tv/feedthebrownie) and X (https://x.com/Feedthebrownies)
- [Privacy](privacy.html) and [Terms](terms.html)
- [Addresses](deployments/1.json): contract addresses as JSON

## API

- POST /v1/chat/completions (OpenAI format, streaming supported)
- GET /v1/models
- POST /v1/auth/challenge {wallet}, then POST /v1/auth/key {nonce, signature}: sign in for a key (no key needed)
- GET /v1/key
- POST /v1/key/rotate (every key of the wallet stops working, and the grants the wallet gave end)
- GET /v1/grants, POST /v1/grants {grantee, daily_usd}, POST /v1/grants/revoke {grantee}: let another wallet spend from your balance up to a daily cap; the spender adds the header X-Brownies-Pay-From: <your wallet>
- GET /api/protocol/account/{wallet}
- GET /api/protocol/stats
- The team adds skills and brownies directly, no vote; the brownies can hire a new brownie themselves when a job is uncovered (a role, tasks and tools, never code). Stakers' votes only decide paid skills they propose.
